one_line: Verified: economics honours thesis on Boston's Jan-2019 STR occupancy tax with committed derived panels - long_reservation_date_by_month/week/sm.csv (city-month/week rows: month, price, nights, unit, trt across Boston plus Asheville, Chicago, Denver, Montreal, Nashville, Providence/RI, Quebec City, San Francisco, Twin Cities, Washington DC), long_date_booked(.2).csv (booking-date aggregation), entries.csv/exits.csv, control_cities.xlsx (tax rates and enactment dates), plus notebooks including 'Panel Data estimation for imputed nights from reviews.ipynb' and 'Validate Transactions.ipynb', writeup.pdf (668 KB) and synth.R; data CSVs are tiny (3-17 KB each), repo bulk is a 12 MB pptx and a 9 MB .pages; no LICENSE; last push 29 Apr 2020 (scout's '2024-04-13' was wrong - that is an update-log day, not a commit date).
abnb_use: Gap #2/#3: an imputed realised-nights and average-price panel by city-month for 11 North American markets in 2018-2019, built from calendar snapshots and cross-validated against review counts (the README reports ~0.5 reviews per imputed night, i.e. ~4 nights per review at the month level) - a direct external calibration of our own reviews-based stays index and a worked template for lodging-tax event studies (gap #12), with the control-city tax-rate sheet usable in the regulatory factor database.
sample_plan: curl -sL from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sideye/airbnb-occupancy-tax/master/ for: long_reservation_date_by_month.csv, long_reservation_date_by_week.csv, long_reservation_date_by_sm_final.csv, long_date_booked.csv, long_date_booked_2.csv, entries.csv, exits.csv, date_normalization.csv, control_cities.xlsx, writeup.pdf, compute_reservations.py, compute_bookings_cutoff.py, synth.R, and 'Panel%20Data%20estimation%20for%20imputed%20nights%20from%20reviews.ipynb'. Total under 1 MB. SKIP Prelim SCM.pptx (12 MB), writeup.pages (9 MB), SCM Analysis.ipynb (1.7 MB). Do NOT run compute_reservations.py or any scraper - the author scraped listing calendars himself; that is a human terms-of-service call.
